details: Individual developmental aspirations vary based on socio-economic background, life situations, and immediate priorities.
Development for one individual or group may not be development for another, and can often be destructive for others.
evidence_or_examples: Industrialists desiring large dams for hydroelectricity vs. indigenous tribal communities facing displacement and loss of agrarian livelihoods.
Urban high-rise real estate expansion displacing local informal slum communities.

branches.theme: 1.2 Material Income & Non-Material Life Quality Goals

details: Besides regular and higher income, people seek non-material aspects of life essential for human dignity and well-being.
Key non-material goals include equal treatment, personal freedom, physical security, respect from others, non-discrimination, and safe working environment.
Women engaging in paid employment gain social dignity, which requires family acceptance, safety, and shared domestic responsibilities.
evidence_or_examples: Job offers considering distance, working atmosphere, and family security over mere monetary salary.
Female labor force participation improving household gender equality.

sub_branches.concept: Per Capita Income & World Bank Criteria
details: National development entails making fair, just, and inclusive choices benefiting the majority of citizens.
World Bank's World Development Reports compare nations using Per Capita Income (PCI = Total National Income / Total Population).
Thresholds (2021): High-income / Rich countries > USD 49,300 per annum; Low-income countries <= USD 2,500 per annum; India is Low-Middle Income (~USD 2,370/year).
evidence_or_examples: World Development Report classification table comparing high, middle, and low-income economies.
Country A vs. Country B comparison showing equal average income ($10,000) but extreme wealth concentration in Country B (one rich citizen earning $48,000 while four earn $500).

sub_branches.concept: UNDP Human Development Indicators vs. Income
details: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Human Development Report, ranking countries on health, education, and GNI per capita.
State-level comparison in India: Haryana has higher Per Capita Income (₹2,36,147) than Kerala (₹2,21,904), but Kerala excels in health and education metrics.
Key Indicators: Infant Mortality Rate (Kerala 7 vs Haryana 30 per 1,000), Literacy Rate (Kerala 94% vs Haryana 80%), Net Attendance Ratio (Kerala 83% vs Haryana 61%).
Public Facilities: Collective provisions like Public Distribution System (PDS), public health centers, and state education cannot be replaced solely by individual private money.
evidence_or_examples: Tamil Nadu PDS reaching 90% rural population resulting in superior health/nutritional status compared to states with weak PDS.
Body Mass Index (BMI = Weight kg / [Height m]²) used as an adult health metric (<18.5 undernourished, >=25 overweight).

details: Sustainable development ensures present growth does not compromise the capabilities and natural assets of future generations.
Renewable resources (groundwater) replenish naturally, but over-exploitation leads to critical water table decline.
Non-renewable resources (crude oil, fossil fuels) have fixed global stocks and will be exhausted within decades at current consumption rates.
evidence_or_examples: Groundwater depletion in 1/3rd of Indian districts (over-pumping in agricultural regions of Punjab, Western UP, and hard-rock plateau areas of Central India).
Mahatma Gandhi's statement: 'The Earth has enough resources to meet the needs of all, but not enough to satisfy the greed of even one person.'
